records.label: Cahokia and American Bottom regional population estimate
rejection_reasons: Illinois State Archaeological Survey distinguishes a roughly 20,000-person six-square-mile urban core from a regional population greater than 50,000; the source does not provide a single rural boundary whose local-food population and saturation can be separated from the city and exchange network.

The American Bottom floodplain is a heterogeneous set of oxbows, wetlands, uplands and rural settlements; assigning the core estimate to all EU5 Cahokia-province cells would silently turn a city/trade observation into surrounding-land capacity.
The 2024 climate-population paper documents flood and drought sensitivity but does not establish a two-sided Malthusian saturation interval.
records.notes: Retain as a research queue item and qualitative floodplain/agriculture test. A future packet may promote a bounded rural survey only after the boundary is reconstructed independently of the Cahokia urban core.

records.label: Kahikinui/Haleakala marginal dryland farming system, Maui
rejection_reasons: Kirch et al. (PNAS 101, 2004, pp. 9936-9941) report peak density of 43-57 persons/km2 only for an incompletely bounded productive zone, with more than 3,000 archaeological features; no total population interval for a mappable EU5 footprint is supplied.

Kirch et al. (2005, pp. 248-254) estimate sustainable sweet-potato output of about 3.2 Mg/ha/year for the sampled complex and document nutrient depletion, but a yield is not itself a population target without a defensible area, diet and non-farm food budget.
The density peak is AD 1700-1800, outside the 1337 technology/date target and affected by contact-era demographic change.
records.notes: Keep the yield and soil-depletion evidence for physical-feature validation, but do not invent a population interval or train on a density copied into the whole Maui location.

records.label: Casarabe managed landscape, Llanos de Mojos
rejection_reasons: The LiDAR study area is approximately 5,020 km2, but the population envelope is extrapolated from settlement visibility and is not an enumeration or saturation interval.
The current EU5 Moxos location contains only a coarse fraction of the study landscape; coverage is approximately 0.2 and cannot supervise an aggregate target.
Seasonally flooded forest islands, canals and managed fisheries establish a valuable physical analogue, not a defensible 1337 Malthusian equilibrium label.
records.notes: Retain for model stress tests of wetland fisheries, raised fields, forest management and seasonal flooding after a precise archaeological-to-EU5 polygon is built.

records.label: Upper Xingu managed landscape
rejection_reasons: The archaeological evidence is distributed across geoglyph, road, ring-village and anthropogenic-soil polygons rather than one historical administrative or ecological boundary.
Regional population values depend on settlement visibility and broad extrapolation and cannot be separated from post-contact epidemic and migration effects.
No EU5 selector currently reaches 95% of the named study polygons without substituting an entire Amazonian macro-region.
records.notes: Keep as a qualitative land-management and human-footprint validation case. Do not train until the distributed polygons are mapped and the local-food interval is independently bounded.
